You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps. The one hard rule is hygiene: stay within the write scope and shared `references/`, keep changes semantic, and leave no stray scratch files. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):

- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, hold a 1-to-1 correspondence with the Lean, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. Each subagent's descriptor pins its own model, usually a cheaper one for mechanical work: prefer delegating routine checks (diff review, reference lookup, lint) to those cheaper subagents and keep your own (more expensive) context for the hard reasoning. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

12	/-!
13	# The Serre twisting sheaf `O(m)` on the integral model of projective space
14	
15	Mathlib v4.31 has no twisted structure sheaf on `Proj`.  This file constructs
16	`O(m)` on the integral model `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]` of projective space as a
17	`SheafOfModules`, by gluing the trivial line bundles on the basic opens
18	`D₊(Xᵢ)` along the transition units `(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)^m`, through the project descent
19	engine `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.glue` (`Picard/GlueDescent.lean`) —
20	the same pattern as the Grassmannian universal quotient
21	(`Picard/GrassmannianQuot.lean`), in rank one.
22	
23	Main definitions:
24	
25	* `ProjTwist.basicOpenCover n` — the open cover of `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ]` by the
26	  `D₊(Xᵢ)`;
27	* `ProjTwist.awayUnit n i j` — the unit `Xᵢ/Xⱼ` of the degree-zero localized
28	  ring `(ℤ[Xᵢ]_{XᵢXⱼ})₀`, and `ProjTwist.overlapUnit n i j` its image in
29	  `Γ(V(i,j), O)` on the scheme-theoretic overlap of the cover;
30	* `ProjTwist.twistTransition n m i j` — the rank-one transition isomorphism
31	  multiplication by `(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)^m`, conjugated by the structure-sheaf pullback
32	  comparison `Modules.pullbackUnitIso`;
33	* `ProjTwist.serreTwist n m` — `O(m)` on `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]`, the glued
34	  sheaf of modules transported along the cover isomorphism `fromGlued`.
35	
36	The convention is that the transition *from* the `i`-th trivialisation *to*
37	the `j`-th multiplies by `(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)^m`, corresponding to the local generator
38	`Xᵢ^m` of `O(m)` on `D₊(Xᵢ)`.
39	
40	Blueprint: `def:serre_twist`, `lem:serre_twist_transition_unit`,
41	`lem:serre_twist_cocycle` (`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
42	-/

57	/-- The variable `Xᵢ` is homogeneous of degree `1`. -/
58	lemma X_mem_deg_one (i : n) :
59	    (X i : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈ homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 1 :=
60	  isHomogeneous_X _ _
61	
62	/-- The product `XᵢXⱼ` is homogeneous of degree `2`. -/
63	lemma X_mul_X_mem_deg_two (i j : n) :
64	    (X i * X j : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
65	      homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 2 :=
66	  SetLike.mul_mem_graded (X_mem_deg_one n i) (X_mem_deg_one n j)

68	/-- The basic opens `D₊(Xᵢ)` cover `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]`: the variables
69	generate the coordinate ring over its degree-zero part. -/
70	lemma iSup_basicOpen_X_eq_top :
71	    ⨆ i, Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i) = ⊤ := by
72	  refine Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' _ _ (fun i => ⟨1, X_mem_deg_one n i⟩) ?_
73	  rw [eq_top_iff]
74	  rintro a -
75	  have ha : a ∈ Algebra.adjoin (ULift.{u} ℤ)
76	      (Set.range (X : n → MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))) := by
77	    rw [MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X]; trivial
78	  induction ha using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
79	  | mem x hx => exact Algebra.subset_adjoin hx
80	  | algebraMap r =>
81	      have hr : (algebraMap (ULift.{u} ℤ) (MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))) r
82	          ∈ homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0 := by
83	        rw [MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq]
84	        exact isHomogeneous_C _ _
85	      exact Subalgebra.algebraMap_mem
86	        (Algebra.adjoin (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)
87	          (Set.range (X : n → MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
88	        (⟨_, hr⟩ : homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)
89	  | add x y _ _ hx hy => exact add_mem hx hy
90	  | mul x y _ _ hx hy => exact mul_mem hx hy

92	/-- The open cover of the integral model by the basic opens `D₊(Xᵢ)`. -/
93	def basicOpenCover :
94	    (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))).OpenCover where
95	  I₀ := n
96	  X i := (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i)).toScheme
97	  f i := (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i)).ι
98	  mem₀ := by
99	    rw [Scheme.presieve₀_mem_precoverage_iff]
100	    refine ⟨fun x => ?_, inferInstance⟩
101	    have : x ∈ ⨆ i, Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i) := by
102	      rw [iSup_basicOpen_X_eq_top]; trivial
103	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp this
104	    exact ⟨i, ⟨x, hi⟩, rfl⟩

106	/-- The glue datum of the basic-open cover of the integral model. -/
107	@[reducible] def glueData : Scheme.GlueData.{u} := (basicOpenCover n).gluedCover
108	
109	/-- The fraction `Xᵢ/Xⱼ = Xᵢ²/(XᵢXⱼ)` as an element of the degree-zero
110	localized ring `(ℤ[X]_{XᵢXⱼ})₀`. -/
111	def awayFraction (i j : n) :
112	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j) :=
113	  Away.mk _ (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two n i j) 1 (X i * X i)
114	    (by simpa using X_mul_X_mem_deg_two n i i)
115	
116	/-- The fraction `Xⱼ/Xᵢ = Xⱼ²/(XᵢXⱼ)` in the *same* localized ring
117	`(ℤ[X]_{XᵢXⱼ})₀` — the inverse of `awayFraction`. -/
118	def awayFractionInv (i j : n) :
119	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j) :=
120	  Away.mk _ (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two n i j) 1 (X j * X j)
121	    (by simpa using X_mul_X_mem_deg_two n j j)
122	
123	lemma awayFraction_mul_inv (i j : n) :
124	    awayFraction n i j * awayFractionInv n i j = 1 := by
125	  apply HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective
126	  rw [HomogeneousLocalization.val_mul, HomogeneousLocalization.val_one,
127	    awayFraction, awayFractionInv, Away.val_mk, Away.val_mk, Localization.mk_mul]
128	  have hnum : (X i * X i) * (X j * X j)
129	      = ((X i * X j) ^ 1 * (X i * X j) ^ 1 : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) := by
130	    ring
131	  rw [hnum]
132	  exact Localization.mk_self
133	    ((⟨(X i * X j) ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ :
134	        Submonoid.powers (X i * X j : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))) *
135	      (⟨(X i * X j) ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ :
136	        Submonoid.powers (X i * X j : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
137	
138	/-- The fraction `Xᵢ/Xⱼ` as a unit of `(ℤ[X]_{XᵢXⱼ})₀`, with inverse
139	`Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. -/
140	def awayUnit (i j : n) :
141	    (Away (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j))ˣ where
142	  val := awayFraction n i j
143	  inv := awayFractionInv n i j
144	  val_inv := awayFraction_mul_inv n i j
145	  inv_val := (mul_comm _ _).trans (awayFraction_mul_inv n i j)

147	/-! ## The transition units on the scheme-theoretic overlaps -/
148	
149	/-- The scheme-theoretic overlap of the glue datum factors through the basic
150	open `D₊(XᵢXⱼ) = D₊(Xᵢ) ⊓ D₊(Xⱼ)`. -/
151	lemma range_overlap_le (i j : n) :
152	    Set.range (pullback.fst ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f j) ≫
153	        (basicOpenCover n).f i).base ⊆
154	      Set.range ((Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))
155	        (X i * X j)).ι).base := by
156	  rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι, Proj.basicOpen_mul]
157	  rintro _ ⟨v, rfl⟩
158	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
159	  · have hx : ((pullback.fst _ _ ≫ (basicOpenCover n).f i) v : Proj _) ∈
160	        Set.range ⇑((Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))
161	          (X i)).ι) := by
162	      rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
163	      exact ⟨_, rfl⟩
164	    exact (Scheme.Opens.range_ι _) ▸ hx
165	  · have hcond := congrArg (fun (φ : pullback ((basicOpenCover n).f i)
166	        ((basicOpenCover n).f j) ⟶ Proj (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))) =>
167	          φ.base v) pullback.condition
168	    simp only at hcond
169	    rw [hcond]
170	    have hx : ((pullback.snd _ _ ≫ (basicOpenCover n).f j) v : Proj _) ∈
171	        Set.range ⇑((Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))
172	          (X j)).ι) := by
173	      rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
174	      exact ⟨_, rfl⟩
175	    exact (Scheme.Opens.range_ι _) ▸ hx

177	/-- The canonical morphism from the scheme-theoretic overlap of the `i`-th and
178	`j`-th charts to the basic open `D₊(XᵢXⱼ)`. -/
179	def overlapHom (i j : n) :
180	    pullback ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f j) ⟶
181	      (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j)).toScheme :=
182	  IsOpenImmersion.lift
183	    ((Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j)).ι)
184	    (pullback.fst ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f j) ≫
185	      (basicOpenCover n).f i)
186	    (range_overlap_le n i j)

188	/-- The ring homomorphism carrying degree-zero fractions over `XᵢXⱼ` to
189	sections of the structure sheaf on the scheme-theoretic overlap. -/
190	def overlapRingHom (i j : n) :
191	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j) →+*
192	      Γ(pullback ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f j), ⊤) :=
193	  ((overlapHom n i j).appTop.hom.comp
194	    ((Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))
195	      (X i * X j)).topIso.inv.hom)).comp
196	    (Proj.awayToSection (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i * X j)).hom
197	
198	/-- The transition unit `(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)` as a unit of the sections of the structure
199	sheaf on the scheme-theoretic overlap of the `i`-th and `j`-th charts. -/
200	def overlapUnit (i j : n) :
201	    Γ(pullback ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f j), ⊤)ˣ :=
202	  Units.map (overlapRingHom n i j).toMonoidHom (awayUnit n i j)

204	/-! ## Rank-one transitions -/
205	
206	/-- A unit of the global sections induces an automorphism of the structure
207	sheaf, multiplication by the unit (rank-one `matrixToFreeIso`). -/
208	def unitScalarIso {Y : Scheme.{u}} (v : Γ(Y, ⊤)ˣ) :
209	    SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf ≅ SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf where
210	  hom := scalarEnd v.val
211	  inv := scalarEnd v.inv
212	  hom_inv_id := by rw [scalarEnd_comp, v.val_inv, scalarEnd_one]
213	  inv_hom_id := by rw [scalarEnd_comp, v.inv_val, scalarEnd_one]
214	
215	@[simp]
216	lemma unitScalarIso_one {Y : Scheme.{u}} :
217	    unitScalarIso (1 : Γ(Y, ⊤)ˣ) = Iso.refl _ :=
218	  Iso.ext (by rw [Iso.refl_hom]; exact (congrArg scalarEnd Units.val_one).trans scalarEnd_one)
219	
220	/-- Iso-level structure-sheaf-pullback cancellation: for equal base morphisms,
221	`pullbackUnitIso φ ≪≫ (pullbackUnitIso ψ).symm` is the `eqToIso` transport
222	(the rank-one analogue of `pullbackFreeIso_trans_symm_eqToIso`). -/
223	lemma pullbackUnitIso_trans_symm_eqToIso {T' T : Scheme.{u}} {φ ψ : T' ⟶ T} (h : φ = ψ) :
224	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso φ ≪≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ψ).symm
225	      = eqToIso (congrArg
226	          (fun α => (Scheme.Modules.pullback α).obj
227	            (SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf)) h) := by
228	  subst h; simp

230	/-- The fraction `Xᵢ/Xᵢ` is `1`. -/
231	lemma awayFraction_self (i : n) : awayFraction n i i = 1 := by
232	  apply HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective
233	  rw [HomogeneousLocalization.val_one, awayFraction, Away.val_mk]
234	  have hden : (⟨(X i * X i) ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ :
235	      Submonoid.powers (X i * X i : MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
236	      = ⟨X i * X i, 1, pow_one _⟩ := Subtype.ext (pow_one _)
237	  rw [hden]
238	  exact Localization.mk_self_mk _ _

240	lemma awayUnit_self (i : n) : awayUnit n i i = 1 :=
241	  Units.ext (awayFraction_self n i)

243	lemma overlapUnit_self (i : n) : overlapUnit n i i = 1 := by
244	  rw [overlapUnit, awayUnit_self, map_one]

246	/-- The rank-one transition isomorphism of the Serre twist `O(m)`:
247	multiplication by `(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)^m`, conjugated by the structure-sheaf pullback
248	comparisons on the scheme-theoretic overlap. -/
249	def twistTransition (m : ℕ) (i j : n) :
250	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((glueData n).f i j)).obj
251	        (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U i).ringCatSheaf) ≅
252	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((glueData n).t i j ≫ (glueData n).f j i)).obj
253	        (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U j).ringCatSheaf) :=
254	  Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).f i j) ≪≫
255	    unitScalarIso ((overlapUnit n i j) ^ m) ≪≫
256	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).t i j ≫ (glueData n).f j i)).symm
257	
258	/-- **(C1)** The diagonal transition of the Serre twist is the canonical
259	cast: `Xᵢ/Xᵢ = 1`, so the scalar automorphism is the identity and the two
260	pullback comparisons cancel. -/
261	lemma twistTransition_self (m : ℕ) (i : n) :
262	    twistTransition n m i i
263	      = eqToIso (congrArg
264	          (fun φ => (Scheme.Modules.pullback φ).obj
265	            (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U i).ringCatSheaf))
266	          (show (glueData n).f i i = (glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i by
267	            rw [(glueData n).t_id i, Category.id_comp])) := by
268	  have hmid : unitScalarIso ((overlapUnit n i i) ^ m)
269	      = Iso.refl (SheafOfModules.unit
270	          (pullback ((basicOpenCover n).f i) ((basicOpenCover n).f i)).ringCatSheaf) := by
271	    rw [overlapUnit_self, one_pow, unitScalarIso_one]
272	  calc twistTransition n m i i
273	      = Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).f i i) ≪≫
274	          unitScalarIso ((overlapUnit n i i) ^ m) ≪≫
275	          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso
276	            ((glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i)).symm := rfl
277	    _ = Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).f i i) ≪≫
278	          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso
279	            ((glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i)).symm := by
280	        refine (congrArg (fun e =>
281	          Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).f i i) ≪≫ e ≪≫
282	            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso
283	              ((glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i)).symm) hmid).trans ?_
284	        exact congrArg (fun e => Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso ((glueData n).f i i) ≪≫ e)
285	          (Iso.refl_trans _)
286	    _ = eqToIso (congrArg
287	          (fun φ => (Scheme.Modules.pullback φ).obj
288	            (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U i).ringCatSheaf))
289	          (show (glueData n).f i i = (glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i by
290	            rw [(glueData n).t_id i, Category.id_comp])) :=
291	      pullbackUnitIso_trans_symm_eqToIso
292	        (show (glueData n).f i i = (glueData n).t i i ≫ (glueData n).f i i by
293	          rw [(glueData n).t_id i, Category.id_comp])

295	/-- **(C2)** The triple-overlap cocycle condition for the Serre-twist
296	transitions, in the exact form consumed by `Scheme.Modules.glue`.  At the
297	level of transition units this is the identity
298	`(Xᵢ/Xⱼ)^m (Xⱼ/Xₖ)^m = (Xᵢ/Xₖ)^m` in `Γ(V(i,j,k), O)`; the remaining work is
299	transporting the conjugated scalar isomorphisms to the triple overlap through
300	the `pullbackUnitIso` coherences (the rank-one analogue of
301	`bundleTransition_cocycle_transport`, `GrassmannianQuot.lean`). -/
302	lemma twistTransition_cocycle (m : ℕ) (i j k : n) :
303	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackBaseChangeTransport
304	        (pullback.fst ((glueData n).f i j) ((glueData n).f i k)) ((glueData n).f i j)
305	        ((glueData n).t i j ≫ (glueData n).f j i) (twistTransition n m i j) ≪≫
306	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
307	        (Scheme.Modules.glueData_bridge_mid (glueData n) i j k)).app
308	          (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U j).ringCatSheaf) ≪≫
309	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackBaseChangeTransport
310	        ((glueData n).t' i j k ≫ pullback.fst ((glueData n).f j k) ((glueData n).f j i))
311	        ((glueData n).f j k) ((glueData n).t j k ≫ (glueData n).f k j)
312	        (twistTransition n m j k) ≪≫
313	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
314	        (Scheme.Modules.glueData_bridge_tgt (glueData n) i j k)).app
315	          (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U k).ringCatSheaf)
316	    = (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
317	        (Scheme.Modules.glueData_bridge_src (glueData n) i j k)).app
318	          (SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n).U i).ringCatSheaf) ≪≫
319	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackBaseChangeTransport
320	        (pullback.snd ((glueData n).f i j) ((glueData n).f i k)) ((glueData n).f i k)
321	        ((glueData n).t i k ≫ (glueData n).f k i) (twistTransition n m i k) := by
322	  sorry

324	/-! ## The Serre twisting sheaf
325	
326	The descent engine `Scheme.Modules.glue` (`Picard/GlueDescent.lean`) is
327	universe-monomorphic at `Scheme.GlueData.{0}` (see the NOTE at
328	`GlueDescent.lean:934`), so the glued sheaf itself is only available for a
329	`Type 0` index — which covers the intended consumers `n = Fin (m + 1)`
330	(`ℙ^m`).  The cover, units and transitions above stay universe-polymorphic
331	for a future generalisation of the engine. -/
332	
333	section Universe0
334	
335	variable (n₀ : Type)
336	
337	/-- The Serre twist `O(m)` on the glued total space of the basic-open cover. -/
338	def serreTwistGlued (m : ℕ) : (glueData n₀).glued.Modules :=
339	  Scheme.Modules.glue (glueData n₀)
340	    (fun i => SheafOfModules.unit ((glueData n₀).U i).ringCatSheaf)
341	    (fun i j => twistTransition n₀ m i j)
342	    (fun i => twistTransition_self n₀ m i)
343	    (fun i j k => twistTransition_cocycle n₀ m i j k)
344	
345	/-- **The Serre twisting sheaf `O(m)`** on the integral model
346	`Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n₀]` of projective space: the glued sheaf transported along
347	the canonical isomorphism `fromGlued`. -/
348	def serreTwist (m : ℕ) :
349	    (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule n₀ (ULift.{0} ℤ))).Modules :=
350	  (Scheme.Modules.pullback (inv (basicOpenCover n₀).fromGlued)).obj
351	    (serreTwistGlued n₀ m)
352	
353	end Universe0

9	/-!
10	# Serre finiteness for the section graded module (statement)
11	
12	The deep remaining input of the Hilbert-polynomial lane
13	(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`, inbox `I-0109`): for a projective scheme over
14	a field carrying a very ample line bundle `L` and a coherent sheaf `F`, the
15	section graded ring `R(X, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, L^{⊗m})` is Noetherian, the section
16	graded module `M(X, F, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite module over it,
